scope: Owner-approved clarification: Brand owns full Appearance identity; independent axes may resolve dependent values.

readback.text:
Core (Primitives) — Literal colors, spacing, typography and radius primitives. One default mode.

Appearance (Brand) — Full visual identity: palette, typography, shape and, where specified, spacing, sizing and other visual properties. Brand A / Brand B / Brand C.

Appearance (Scheme) — Brand-aware light and dark realizations. Light Mode / Dark Mode.

Appearance (Scale) — Scalar projections and fluid endpoints, potentially brand-specific. Current branch: shared Min / Max endpoints.

Semantics (Roles) — Reusable purpose and state contracts. One default mode.

Patterns (UI) — Component family, variant, part, property and state slots. One Component mode.

Interaction (States) — Four prototype helpers. Explicitly excluded from the foundation contract and Runtime projection.

Arrows in the architecture show increasing abstraction. Variable aliases point back toward their dependencies.

Patterns consume Semantics. Semantics consume Appearance. Brand, Scheme and Scale are independently selected context axes; their resolved values can depend on one another. Scheme and Scale may consume Brand or Core. The semantic layer adds stable purpose without selecting the context.

Brand owns the full visual identity: colors, typography, shape and, where specified, spacing, sizing and other visual properties. Scheme selects its light/dark realization; Scale selects its size or responsive realization.

Independent controls do not imply brand-neutral values. Surfaces can depend on Brand × Scheme; typography and layout can depend on Brand × Scale, or all three axes where required. Shared values remain shared when that is intentional.

Core’s qualified Brand A/B/C source palettes identify private provenance. Semantics and Patterns keep stable purpose and slot names across brands. UIF remains separate from UILib.

Min and Max are interpolation endpoints. Scale can be brand-specific: Brand may select typography and layout endpoints while Scale determines their responsive realization.

Current projection limitation: this branch has shared literal Min/Max endpoints and Core bridges. Brand-specific endpoint selection is not implemented yet. A separate bounded contract and parity check are required to add it.

Runtime projects the current Figma endpoints into a global fluid clamp. The corrected lg curve is 20–36px; the former code-only 18–20px Liquid curve is preserved in migration evidence.

Shape is one part of the full Brand-owned Appearance. Brand owns corner choices; Semantics exposes reusable purpose. Patterns share those roles rather than aliasing another component’s radius. Existing brand values and public CSS names remain compatible.
